findings.finding: The main database is first opened by the standard VFS using MAIN_DB and READONLY flags. Only afterwards does Pager interpret immutable and set tempFile=1, eState=PAGER_READER, eLock=EXCLUSIVE_LOCK, noLock=1. This changes pager behavior, not the unix sqlite3_file.pMethods close implementation. Immutable is not a switch to unix-none/nolockClose.

The shared-lock hot-journal and pagerOpenWalIfPresent branch requires PAGER_OPEN, skipped by immutable's initial READER state. pagerOpenWalIfPresent also checks !tempFile. Btree's separate WAL-header path calls sqlite3PagerOpenWal, but its !tempFile&&!pWal guard is false for immutable; pbOpen=1 is returned without opening WAL or SHM.

For the examined read-only probe there is no open journal and pWal remains NULL. WalClose's if(pWal) guard skips checkpoint/WAL/SHM deletion. journal finalization requires an open jfd; no jfd means no journal zero/truncate/delete. Pager noLock suppresses OsUnlock. Main xClose still belongs to the SQLite VFS.
Do not claim immutable automatically sets journal_mode=OFF. The OFF assignment is conditional on !useJournal; the sidecar proof instead depends on tempFile, READER, unopened jfd, and NULL pWal.

Standard POSIX VFS keeps per-inode lock state shared by SQLite connections. Probe's unixFile has acquired no lock, so unixUnlock(NO_LOCK) returns without removing another connection's locks. unixClose defers its descriptor to pUnused and sets h=-1 while inode nLock>0; closeUnixFile does not close negative h. Deferred descriptors close when the last lock clears or last inode reference is released.

This is the normal same-SQLite-instance standard-VFS guarantee, not an absolute guarantee for every I/O failure or custom VFS. SQLite itself immediately closes on fstat failure and its comment acknowledges lock-loss risk; macOS fstatfs failure similarly closes before inode registration. Separate SQLite library instances do not share inode bookkeeping. Application raw File open/read/drop must not be reintroduced.

READONLY VFS main-file open requests GENERIC_READ and OPEN_EXISTING without DELETE_ON_CLOSE. xRead uses ReadFile; main xClose uses CloseHandle. Windows byte-range locks attach to file handles. This inspection contains no Windows runtime execution or filesystem fault injection.

PRAGMA schema_version reaches a Btree page-1 read and header checks; it is not literally a direct 100-byte-only xRead. NOTADB is a conservative main-file format rejection. Immutable omits WAL and locking/change-detection, so it cannot establish the current WAL snapshot or full store health. A concurrently changing main can produce incorrect results or errors; observed non-NOTADB errors in the retained-sidecar branch are deliberately delegated to the existing WAL-aware opener, not claimed as health acceptance.

A fresh private pager is a premise: a globally enabled shared cache may reuse another BtShared/pager. PRIVATE_CACHE/cache=private can make that premise explicit if chosen by integrator. SQLite auto-extension callbacks run when opening connections and may execute arbitrary extension code. Our default-branch and available-local-source searches found no registration symbols, but are not a complete exact-5c285 negative proof. No global setting or extension was reset or mutated.

Examined production probe still returns Ok for missing main and admits zero-byte main even with retained sidecars; fix must stat-refuse missing/zero main with retained sidecars before any SQLite open.
